_README: Triaged, benign title divergences between a sprint-plan heading and the
Why this file exists: the crosswalk accumulates outcomes over time (a title
grows '- rec: keep v3' once the work lands) while plan headings stay as
written at sprint start. That benign drift produced enough noise to hide a
REAL key reuse (AINOS3-30, Sprint 27) for ten days. Acknowledging the benign
cases keeps the noise floor at zero so a real one is visible immediately.
Add an entry ONLY after confirming the plan and the crosswalk describe the
SAME work. If they describe different work the key has been reused - split
the new work under its own slug instead of acknowledging it here.
23:AINOS3-30: Same work. Plan names the goal ('recover DEAD classes'), crosswalk names the mechanism ('subscribe extra MIDs'). Legitimate carryover of one scope; only Sprint 27 changed it, which is now split to AINOS3-88.
23:AINOS3-44: Same work. Crosswalk specifies the mechanism (reconstruction-error) the plan leaves implicit.
23:AINOS3-46: Same work. Crosswalk appends the tier detail (live execution / agent).
24:AINOS3-39: Same work. Crosswalk appends the OUTCOME ('rec: keep v3'), which the plan heading predates.
24:AINOS3-40: Same work. Crosswalk appends where the explanations surface (incident + demo).
24:AINOS3-69: Same work. Crosswalk appends the decision framing (Phase 5/6 vs consolidate).
26:AINOS3-68: Same work. Crosswalk appends the gating condition (after AINOS3-30 broadens signal).
26:AINOS3-70: Same work. Crosswalk appends the specifics (16 MIDs, pipe cap 32->48, 383 cols).
26:AINOS3-71: SCOPE CORRECTED, same ticket. Plan says 'DS/FM'; the sprint found the DS premise wrong (DS.FileWriteCounter climbs in nominal and would false-positive) and shipped FM-only. Crosswalk records the corrected scope. Not a reuse - the ticket delivered what it set out to, by a different field.

26:AINOS3-75: Same work. Crosswalk names the three held-outs the plan refers to collectively.
